beats.story: I follow Gregory like a scorned child. Clifford strolls behind me, whispering chipper hellos to the tilting heads we pass. Eight years of doing everything I could to remain invisible here, and this is what it comes to. There were days when not one person said a word to me. I'd come in, put on my headphones, have a lunch-hour cry alone in the bathroom, then clock out. Eight years, and now it's like I've lost a layer of skin. As my desk pod comes into view, Garret crouches over Caitlin's cubicle wall and mouths something that draws Caitlin's stare toward me. I focus on my breathing, on my footing.
beats.story_cn: 我像个被羞辱的孩子般跟在格雷戈里身后。克利福德在我身后闲庭信步，对沿途颔首致意的人们低声打着轻快的招呼。我在这里苦熬八年，千方百计让自己隐形，最终竟落得这般田地。曾经连一整天都无人与我说半句话。我总是戴上耳机走进办公室，独自在洗手间里吃掉午餐顺便哭上一场，然后准时打卡下班。整整八年，此刻却仿佛活生生被剥去一层皮。当我的工位隔间映入眼帘时，加勒特正趴在凯特琳的隔板墙上，用嘴型传递着什么，引得凯特琳的目光射向我。我专注调节呼吸，稳住脚步。

beats.story: Garret is Caitlin's best friend, and not by coincidence. As the head of business development, he's Gregory's second-in-command, and he is always sharing insider information with Caitlin. As a person, he's like the human embodiment of an internet comments section. Caitlin can't suppress her grin when she spots our parade. I get it; this situation is her big break. I live for this from the other side of it. But right now, I'd love to remind her about the time she got drunk at our Christmas party two years ago and rubbed against the guy who was cutting ham slices at the buffet. Also, the party took place here in the office at three p.m.
beats.story_cn: 加勒特是凯特琳最好的朋友，绝非偶然。作为业务开发部主管，他是格雷戈里的副手，总与凯特琳分享内部消息。就为人而言，他活像网络评论区的人格化身。凯特琳瞥见我们的队列时忍不住咧嘴笑了。我懂：这局面是她的绝佳舞台。我曾在另一侧为这种时刻痴狂。但此刻，我真想提醒她两年前圣诞派对上喝得酩酊大醉，在自助餐台前蹭着切火腿片那个男人的模样——顺便一提，那派对是在下午三点，就在这间办公室里举办的。

beats.story: The highlight of the event was the secret Santa. Some legend, in a brazenly genius move, took a piece of crappy office stock art off the wall outside of Gregory's office and wrapped it up for him. Nobody knows who it was, but I'd have paid a month's rent to see Gregory's face when he opened it again. Gregory halts and loudly proclaims, "Everyone, this is our new HR analyst, Cliff. He'll be shadowing some of our processes to learn more about what we do here." Then he nudges Cliff in the side, who doesn't hide his flinch. "Don't worry. He won't be spying on everyone that much." Cliff's eyelids droop to half-mast, which I appreciate, as whispers creep over the cubicle walls. He clenches his jaw before saying, "I'm here for any concerns you might have, so please feel free to come by and say hello." And I don't know if I want to hug him for diverting some of the attention away from me or jab him in the kidney for drawing more looks in our general direction.
beats.story_cn: 活动高潮当属秘密圣诞环节。某位传奇同事竟做出厚颜无耻又天才的举动——从格雷戈里办公室门外墙上摘下一幅蹩脚公司库存装饰画，精心包装后赠予他。无人知晓始作俑者是谁，但我愿赌上一个月房租只为重见格雷戈里拆礼物时的表情。此时格雷戈里驻足高声宣布：“各位，这位是新任人力资源分析师克利夫，他将跟随观摩部分流程以熟悉业务。”说罢用手肘轻推克利夫，后者明显瑟缩。“放心，他不会过度监视各位。”克利夫半垂眼睑的神情令我暗自称许，此时窃窃私语已漫过隔间矮墙。他紧咬牙关补充道：“诸位若有任何疑虑，随时欢迎前来沟通。”我竟分不清是该感谢他分散了投向我的注意力，还是该给他肾上来一拳——毕竟现在更多目光正朝我们这个角落聚集。

beats.story: When we're finally at my cubicle, Gregory huddles closer. "I'm not needed for this part." He places his hand on my shoulder -- I've lost track of how many times I've been touched against my will by this man -- and nudges Cliff once more. "You'll take it from here? She can wait there." He points at a spot right next to my garbage bin. Blinking eyes are peering over all the cube walls like owls. The new HR guy. My computer. It's too much for these people.
beats.story_cn: 好不容易挪到我的小隔间，格雷戈里又凑得更近。“这部分我不用在场。”他把手搭在我肩上——这男人未经我允许多少次上手了，我早已数不清——又推了推克里夫。“后面交给你？她可以待在那儿。”他指指紧挨我垃圾桶的一块地方。隔板墙后眨巴眨巴的眼睛像猫头鹰似的探出来张望。新来的HR。我的电脑。这帮人简直看呆了。

beats.story: Clifford sends me another apologetic smile. Pointless. I stare at some unknown beige stain on the seat of my chair that I never much minded until now. Then Gregory's gone, and Cliff, who seems to dwarf my entire desk area, covers the mouse with his hand. After thirty seconds or twelve hours, Cliff says, "So, any big plans for the birthday weekend?" No. Not the questions. Not from this HR analyst. I try to keep any emotion from my voice as I reply, "Can we not?" "Sure." He nods as his grin evaporates.
beats.story_cn: 克利福德又冲我挤了个歉疚的笑。白搭。我盯着椅面上一块米乎乎的渍印——以前压根没在意过——直到此刻才扎眼。接着格雷戈里闪人了，克里夫，他那身板衬得我整张桌子都缩了水似的，拿手把鼠标一捂。过了半分钟还是半辈子，克里夫开口：“生日周末有啥大计划？”不行。别来这套。更别从这HR分析师嘴里问。我答话时拼命压住情绪：“能不提吗？”“成。”他点头，笑容瞬间蒸发。

beats.story: I force my attention on a loose plasticky thread pulling up from a seam in the grey office carpet. Guilt is pointless right now. The office drifts back into silence, aside from a few throats clearing and chairs shuffling and too-rhythmic clacking on keyboards, all the noises someone makes when they're fake working. Eventually Cliff lifts himself from my chair and says, "You're all set. Would you like to see what I've done?" Because I know everything, I mutter, "I'm good," and shrink further into the collar of my sweater. "Okay. I feel like I need to warn you that if your emails contain certain words, they'll be flagged and sent to management -- so tread lightly." His smile curls up, all cheeky, as he leans in conspiringly. "Also, your browser will block certain searches and websites." His fresh-linen scent lingers past his words.
beats.story_cn: 我强迫自己盯住灰色地毯接缝处翘起的一截塑料线头。此刻愧疚毫无意义。办公室恢复沉寂，只余几声清嗓、椅子挪动和键盘过于规律的敲击——全是人们假模假式工作时制造的动静。最终克利夫从我的椅子上起身说道："都搞定了。要看看我做了什么吗？"因我早知一切，只含糊应声"不用了"，同时把脸更深埋进棉毛衫领口。"行。我觉得有必要提醒你，邮件若含特定词汇会被标记并发送给管理层——所以走钢丝时可得留神。"他凑近时露出顽皮的卷唇笑意，"另外，浏览器会屏蔽某些搜索与网站。"他身上清爽的亚麻气息比话语更绵长。

beats.story: He's speaking in low tones, but still, he needs to keep his voice down. I cannot physically crouch further into myself, and all the stares are churning my stomach. I don't respond. Instead I focus on some random child's demented art that a magnet holds to a filing cabinet behind Rhonda. This place really is in a sad state. The first red flag should have been during my interview, when Gregory said the company was "like family." Cliff lingers. "For what it's worth," he whispers, "I will try and work with you where you're at, to make this as painless as possible. It'll just be constructive ways to get along with people." He grins again, like he's already laughing at the joke he's about to make.
beats.story_cn: 他压低嗓门说话，却依然该把声量再收三分。我已蜷缩到躯体极限，四面八方投来的目光几乎令我翻江倒海。我没有回应，只是死死盯着琳达身后文件柜上用磁铁吸着的——某孩童的癫狂画作。这地方真是没救了。首个危险信号本应出现在面试时，格雷戈里说出“公司像一家人”的瞬间。克里夫仍在徘徊。“说实话，”他耳语道，“我会试着理解你目前的处境，尽量让过程少些痛楚。不过是些帮助你融入集体的建设性建议。”他又咧开嘴笑，仿佛已在为即将抛出的笑话提前喝彩。

beats.story: "I gotta change the rep us HR guys have." My smile isn't that forced. "Thanks." Finally, he walks away, leaving me alone with an hour of work still to go and a dozen eyes burning against my back. I need to plot my revenge on everyone. Because this has sparked joy in their hearts. The thing about working in a regional office for a big-box retailer that sells corn by-products, camping things, and cream for various types of rashes and boils is that not one of us is living our dream. They'll talk about starting a sandwich truck, even though they aren't even qualified to roast a marshmallow, or fleeing to Belize to teach surfing lessons. But every one of them shows up on Monday, until the weeks turn into a life sentence. My situation is the only beauty left in life for them.
beats.story_cn: “得扭转外界对咱们HR的刻板印象了。”我的笑容还算自然。“多谢。”他终于走开，留我独自面对一小时未竟的工作，以及数十道灼烧后背的视线。我得谋划场复仇大戏，因为我的窘态正是他们的快乐源泉。在这家售卖玉米副产品、露营装备和各式皮疹药膏的大型零售企业区域办事处工作，没有谁真正在追逐梦想。他们谈论着要开流动三明治车——尽管连棉花糖都烧不成炭；或是逃往伯利兹教授冲浪——但每个人都准时在周一现身，直到数周堆叠成终生苦役。而我的处境，已是他们黯淡生活里仅存的风景。

beats.story: The suggestion that I need to get along with people here is actually bonkers. Because that was exactly what I wanted when I first joined this so- called family eight years ago. I was so optimistic that this job would be a fresh start and I'd make friends, move up the ladder, and do what any person would do while working at a place like this. Even when Rhonda showed me to my new pod -- the stained chair, while hers was brand new -- I didn't take the hint that I was entering a stupid game in which the rules are unclear and the prizes are yet unknown. I didn't factor in my anxiety and my complete inability to be a casual person about anything. I failed miserably during my first six months. I had no idea yet about things like: working faster than everyone is bad, actually; not talking about your private life with colleagues is suspicious; and you have to be fake nice to powerful people even when they treat you horribly. When I finally realized that the same situations that caused me so much anxiety in high school had followed me here, I had a panic attack and took four sick days.
beats.story_cn: 说“我需要和同事和睦相处”真是荒谬绝伦。因为这正是我八年前踏进这个所谓“大家庭”时最朴素的愿望。我曾满心期待这份工作能成为人生新起点——结交朋友、步步高升，像所有普通职员那样在职场中安然度日。即便朗达领我到那张污渍斑斑的隔间工位（而她的椅子崭新如初），我也未察觉自己正踏入一场规则模糊、奖惩未卜的愚蠢游戏。我全然忽略了自己的焦虑体质，更不具备对任何事保持淡然的能力。入职头六个月我一败涂地。那时我还不懂：比所有人更努力反而是错；与同事分享私生活会惹人生疑；哪怕位高者待你如敝履，你也得强装奉承。当我终于明白高中时那些令我备受煎熬的境况在此地如影随形时，恐慌症骤然发作，不得不请了四天病假。

beats.story: I almost didn't make it back. I returned because I needed to survive, and this job was the only way I knew how to do that. So I figured out how to keep a low profile, working in silence while everyone hung out around me. I've survived this long, even though I've seen a lot of turnover. Four years ago, Armin's desk used to be occupied by a guy named Harold. And I've seen three other people in Caitlin's role before her: two who moved up the ranks, and one who transferred to another city. I've spent more time with these people than anyone. We're forced to work together in close proximity every day, which really means we're forced to live together.
beats.story_cn: 我差点没能熬回来。回来只为求生，而这份工作是我仅知的生存之道。于是我学会潜伏术——在众人喧哗时静默劳作。尽管见过太多人来来去去，我竟存活至今。四年前阿明的位子还属于叫哈罗德的男人；而在我认识的三位前任凯特琳里，两人升迁远走，一人调去了别的城市。我和这些面孔相处的时间比任何人都长。我们被迫每日贴身共事，这本质上无异于被迫同居共存。

beats.story: And it's the living involved. The sheer humanity of that, which could never be professional, or even normal. We're all dry flecks of skin turning to dust and breathing each other up. It's too much. I never talk to them, yet I know things about them. Every day I put on my headphones, but I listen. Rhonda may brag that her son poops at exactly nine thirty a.m. Eastern Standard Time, but she also steals coffee creamer from the fridge on the sixth floor.
beats.story_cn: 关键在于那些活生生的人。那种纯粹的人性味儿，既不能算职业范畴，甚至都谈不上正常。我们不过是一堆干皮屑终将化为尘埃，互相呼吸着对方的呼吸。这太过了。我从不和他们交谈，却对他们的事了如指掌。每天我都戴上耳机，实则一直在旁听。朗达或许会炫耀她儿子每天东部时间九点半准时排便，可她也会偷拿六楼冰箱里的咖啡奶精。

beats.story: Armin is slowly and intentionally killing Joey, Rhonda's fern that sits between their desks. I've seen him pour blue Gatorade into the soil at least a dozen times. I have a theory why he's committing plant murder (possible revenge for the high crime of unwarranted kabob disposal), but the behavior is still unhinged. Mel Elliot has an outfit routine that is disturbingly precise. Blue cardigan and beige skirt every Monday, painful-looking shoes every Friday. Ron McDowell lost access to the shared drive last month and has opted to try to live without it by simply working way less. Nobody has noticed. And Mary Perkins has a literal plank and hammer in her office that she crushes walnuts with.
beats.story_cn: 阿明正缓慢而蓄意地谋杀着朗达养在办公桌间的那盆蕨类植物“乔伊”。我至少见过十几次他往土里倒蓝色佳得乐。关于他为何犯下这起植物谋杀案，我有个猜想（可能是对随意丢弃烤肉串这一重罪的报复），但这行为依然十分疯癫。梅尔·埃利奥特的着装规律精确得令人不安：每周一必是蓝开衫配米色裙子，每周五必定是那双看着就疼的鞋子。罗恩·麦克道尔上个月失去了共享驱动器的访问权限，于是干脆选择少干许多活来适应没有它的日子。根本没人发现。玛丽·帕金斯办公室里居然真放着木板和锤子，用来砸核桃。

beats.story: It sounds like she's doing a murder every afternoon, yet we all zombie-stare at our spreadsheets of data without flinching at the batshit noises. I didn't choose a single person here and never would've, yet I'm spending my life with them. "Where's the accounts paid doc?" Armin asks Rhonda, breaking me from my thoughts. "It's not in the accounts folder?" "If it were in that folder, I wouldn't have asked." With that, our office clicks back into its mundane rhythm. My drama has already dissolved. I'm invisible once again.
beats.story_cn: 听起来她每天下午都在办公室里杀人，可我们全都像僵尸盯屏般对着数据表格麻木不仁，对那些鬼哭狼嚎的动静毫无反应。我从未主动选择这里任何一个人，原本也绝不会与他们共度余生。"报销单据在哪？"阿明问朗达，把我的思绪拽了回来。"不在财务文件夹里？" "如果在那里我就不用问了。"随着这句话，办公室重新点击回它庸常的节奏。我的戏剧性时刻早已消散。我再次成了隐形人。
